answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to a bonded compute island whose hardware and clock fingerprints are remeasured each epoch. Useful reputation is only a short plume of recent, uniquely signed work traces; older traces decay and cannot be copied onto fresh keys. Before an identity may grade or spend, it must complete a tundra of delayed, low-reward tasks under the same fingerprint. Proven clones slash the island bond and evict every linked key, so mass identity farms fail on cost.
